title: Distinguish optional schema resource unavailability from denial
api_or_output: Distinguish optional schema resource unavailability from denial

acceptance.description: Freeze and compile the exact additive result/status/virtual ResolveResult surface in the accepted coordinator brief before runtime implementation. Default result is Denied/null; only a non-null resource factory yields Resolved; legacy Resolve and ResolveAsync declarations and all old API rows remain unchanged. No public stubs.

Implement default synchronous adapter with identical request/token, one legacy callback and null-to-Denied mapping, preserving caller exceptions. Add only a concrete optional loader seam; explicit Unavailable can return absence before Refuse, mandatory Load stays strict, and missing resolver/legacy null/Denied still refuse. Preserve parsing, source identity, quotas/cancellation, ownership and exactly-once disposal. No async or non-schema consumer changes.

Prove default/factory invariants, legacy consumers, explicit unavailable/denied at optional and mandatory sites, exception propagation, cancellation before/after acquisition or unavailable, disposal failures, aggregate resource/work boundaries, redirected bases and shared principal/external parsing. Unavailable cannot create a document/cache entry/fresh budget or evade bounded attempted-work checks.

Pass focused shared-resource and affected validator suites, additive compiled public API and unchanged frozen lane interfaces, normal/true XML-only consumers, task validation and actual bounded allocation evidence using existing infrastructure. Leave XSD directive semantics to the ordered compiler task; no corpus oracle rewriting.

handoff.summary: Planned compatible owning repair after independent source and main scope review; no implementation yet. Exact design: docs/orchestration/brief-M8-schema-resource-outcomes.md.
